messages:
alex: heads up — seeing a surge in stream.disconnects and duplicate session counts in the console after last night's proxy rollout :confused:

alex: console shows ~2x session_open -> session_close pairs for the same session-id, and billing telemetry is spiking for some tenants

alex: sample log snippet:```
INFO proxy: conn close: reason=FIN_SENT session_id=abc123 route=eu-west-1 edge=proxy-12
INFO client: reconnect attempt=1 session_id=abc123 err=early-eof
INFO billing: tokens_charged=120 session_id=abc123
```

sara: was that on the canary? which percent?

alex: canary 7% (edge proxy change that toggles `preemptive_drain=true`). started ~02:15 UTC

mike: I repro locally — when proxy sends FIN and we don't surface a clear Close-Reason, the client immediately opens a new session and server records a new session_open before backend has finished cleaning KV cache -> double charge

mike: looks like the resume token was still valid so client retried and we billed both the tail tokens and the restarted stream tokens

jamie: that matches an old race we've tried to fix. Two ideas: (1) delay billing finalization until the agent confirms session tombstone persisted, or (2) change proxy to send a `X-Stream-Drain: grace_ms` header so client can backoff instead of immediate reconnect

alex: (2) is lower risk short-term. can we add header quickly?

sara: proxy change is small but needs a config toggle. deploy-bot: deployment 2024-11-18T02:10 -> proxy-12 rolled to 7% canary

deploy-bot: @channel rollout note: feature preemptive_drain=true; config key=proxy.preemptive_drain

mike: adding header `X-Stream-Drain: 2000` (2s) reduces dup-charge in my local stress — client waits jitter before opening new socket

jamie: long-term we should change console telemetry: add a per-session tag `session_close_reason={FIN,SOFT_DRAIN,AUTH_FAIL,IDLE}` and expose a small pie/hist in route dashboard. current metric `session_close_total` is too coarse

alex: agreed. ops can't tell whether a close was expected vs crash. also need a metric for "billing_finalized" vs "billing_pending" so we can track duplicates

sara: UX ask: show active drain policy on rollout page. When changing routing policies, list the drain window (ms) and whether it will send header. PMs keep getting surprised by hidden proxy defaults

jamie: also add a console anomaly alert if same session_id shows 2+ separate session_open in <5s — that will catch regressions quickly

mike: small cli snippet to detect dup sessions from logs:```shell
cat proxy.log | jq -r '. | select(.session_id) | [.session_id, .event] | @tsv' | awk '{count[$1]++} END {for (k in count) if (count[k]>1) print k, count[k]}'
```

alex: good. action items: (A) sara to roll proxy toggle back to false for canary until header landed (B) jamie to add session_close_reason tag to telemetry + dashboard panel (C) mike to draft client backoff jitter when X-Stream-Drain present (D) alex to open support incident with cost samples and tenant list

sara: can do A; reverting to 0% now -> deploy-bot: rollback initiated 02:43 UTC

deploy-bot: rollback complete for canary group at 02:44 UTC

jamie: I'll take B — will put a quick panel in route dashboard and add an alert threshold. ETA EOD

mike: I'll open a small PR for client jitter behavior and add tests against `X-Stream-Drain` header. assigning to @mike. ETA tomorrow morning

alex: I'll gather tenant examples and billing deltas, ping support & finance for reconciliation

sara: thanks all. once jamie's panel is up we should run a tight canary with header enabled at 2% and watch the new histograms before broad rollout :thumbsup:

mike: +1 — also suggest we add a one-off meter for `session_reconnects.within_5s` so we can compare pre/post quickly

alex: noted. closing thread when PRs + panel exist.
